general_information.Description: The course covers a sufficient understanding of fundamental physics concepts, and helps students apply this conceptual understanding to quantitative problem solving. It also helps students to perceive underlying physics phenomena through practical lab sessions. Topic covered: Measurements, Mechanics, Thermodynamics, Electromagnetisms, Optics, Quantum Physics and Semiconductors.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend more than 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Students must complete the lab sessions with the average passing grade. - Promptly access to the FU CMS at http://cms.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information
general_information.Tools: Lab equipments for 4 sessions of Mechanics, Thermodynamics, Electromagnetisms and Optics (see Lab manual for more details)

assessments.Question Type: Multiple choice questions or suitable format
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Each Progess Test must cover generally all learned topics of the course.
assessments.Grading Guide: by instructors and by suitable means (computer or paper)
assessments.Note: Instruction and shedules for Progress tests must be presented in the Course Implementation Plan approved by the director of the campus. Instructor has responsibility to review the test for students after graded.

assessments.Question Type: Questions at the end of lab manuals
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: All related main topics: mechanics, thermodynamics, electromagnetisms & semiconductors and optics.
assessments.Grading Guide: - 4 lab sessions are allocated suitably according to specific implementation condition of every campus - groups of 2-3 students are guided by instructors before doing experiments - perform step-by-step measurements or observation following lab manuals and take required data to process afterward. - A average grade of 5 in laboratory is required to pass the course.
assessments.Note: Lab manuals should be given to students at the beginning of the course Be aware that students will not be able to make up the lab. If students miss a lab they must either have a written doctor’s excuse or an excuse approved by your laboratory instructor to avoid having a score of zero recorded for the missed lab. Bring a calculator to the laboratory. The lab reports are normally collected right after the lab session.

assessments.Question Type: follow requirement of appropriate case studies
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: All related main topics: mechanics, thermodynamics, electromagnetisms and optics.
assessments.Grading Guide: - Project 1: Mechanics, work in groups of 3 to 5, to explore an application of mechanical physics into human computer interaction using smart-phones - Project 2: Thermodynamics, work in groups of 2, to explore an application of thermodynamics into data center setup and operation - Project 3: Electromagnetics, work in groups of 5, to explore an application of electromagnetism into energy supply of mobile device - Project 4: Optics, work in groups of 4, to explore an application of optics into computer display Presentation will be held after every project
assessments.Note: - Every project starts with 45 minute instruction and group division - Students are required to share tasks equally, do the project at home and present by group in class. - Reports are made by group and submitted right after presentation. - Results are marked for the whole group and returned to students in approximately 4 days after submission. - Be aware that students will not be able to make up the late submission.

assessments.Question Type: Multiple choice questions marked by computer
assessments.Note: No materials may be consulted during an exam unless specifically permitted by your instructor. A calculator is necessary for exams, but all memory must be erased.
